description:
When frost normally arrives on this ground, and whether it is coming this week.

Returns first-frost dates from the last ten seasons, how far the region's
own terrain spreads that, and a night-by-night assessment of the coming
forecast for the *coldest* ground rather than the average. A season
begins where this ground's own record never frosts — mid-July in Vermont,
mid-January south of the equator — given as ``first_frost.season_starts``.
``this_season`` is the season so far, up to yesterday: its first frost,
or with none yet, ``given_none_yet`` — when the seasons still frost-free
by now went on to frost, which is the answer once the median has passed.

The spread is the answer's point. Frost forms on still, clear nights when
cold air drains off high ground and pools in low, so a single forecast low
is optimistic for a hollow and pessimistic for a bench on the same block.

block.description: The ground to answer for: a block you have saved — its id, its name, one of its aliases, or any part of its name that only one block has (e.g. "Meadow" for "Lower Meadow"). If several match, the error lists them with their ids. Blocks may overlap; each answers for its own ground. Save one with block_save first; geometry travels once, not on every call.

dpop_token.description: Proof that the caller holds npub. Either the grant envelope that receive_npub_proof returned, or the raw JSON of a kind-27235 Nostr event signed by npub: content "", a `u` tag holding this tool's exact name from tools/list, created_at within 60 s of now, and a random `nonce` tag.

npub.description: The patron's Nostr public key (npub1...). Tool fees are paid from this patron's balance; dpop_token proves the caller holds it.
